Theme

# Philosophy quotes about knowledge

Knowledge is the philosophical study of what we can justifiably claim to know—and where certainty ends.

74 passages · 8+ thinkers in this selection

## Why this theme matters

Epistemology asks whether knowledge is justified true belief, reliable tracking of the world, or something else; it also asks how perception, testimony, memory, and reason contribute.

## In the history of philosophy

From Plato’s dialogues and Indian pramāṇa theory to Descartes, Hume, Kant, and contemporary analytic epistemology, the theme remains a core branch of philosophy.

## Thinkers in this collection

[Socrates](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/socrates) , [Augustine of Hippo](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/augustine-of-hippo) , [Michel de Montaigne](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/michel-de-montaigne) , [René Descartes](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/rene-descartes) , [Arthur Schopenhauer](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/arthur-schopenhauer) , [William James](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/william-james) , [Auguste Comte](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/auguste-comte) , [Albert Camus](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/albert-camus)

## Frequently asked questions

### What is knowledge in philosophy?

A leading starting point is justified true belief, refined by debates about Gettier cases, reliability, evidence, and understanding.

### How do philosophers distinguish knowledge from opinion?

By asking for reasons, methods, and standards of evidence that can survive scrutiny—not by intensity of conviction alone.
